Wynn Daily Poker Tournaments 
General Terms and Conditions 
 
1. These General Poker Tournament Terms and Conditions are meant to be read and followed in 
conjunction with Wynn’s standard poker tournament rules, and each individual Tournament event’s 
(may be referred to as “Event” or collectively as a “Tournament”) Terms and Conditions and Structure 
Sheet. In the event there is a conflict, these Terms and Conditions shall prevail. 
 
2. Players and guests must be at least 21 years of age. 
 
3. Registration for each Event will open four (4) hours prior to the scheduled start of play. Players will 
register in the Wynn Las Vegas Poker Room, located in Encore at Wynn Las Vegas. 
 
4. The Tournament entry fee (the “Entry Fee”) must be paid with cash or Wynn Las Vegas live casino 
chips; no other forms of payment will be accepted. 
 
5. All Events will use Tournament chips for play. Tournament chips have no cash value, may not be used 
for any other purpose, and must be returned to Wynn Las Vegas at the end of each Event.   
 
6. All Events will utilize the Big Blind Ante format unless otherwise noted on the Tournament structure 
sheet.  In the event that the player in the big blind has less than the required amount to post both the 
big blind and the ante, the big blind will be posted first. The ante will then be posted with any remaining 
Tournament chips.  
 
7. Tournament chip stacks will be put into play at the start of the event for all registered players who have 
been issued a table and seat assignment. Players registered as an “alternate” will receive a seat 
assignment from the Tournament Staff when seating becomes available. In events where applicable, 
the tournament chip stack of players who have received a discount for early registration will be put into 
play at the start of the event. 
 
8. At the conclusion of the registration period, all paid entries (including alternates) who have yet to be 
seated will be assigned a seat and their Tournament chips will be put into play. 
 
9. A player will forfeit their option to cancel (void) their entry once their Tournament chip stack has been 
put into play and will not be entitled to a refund.   
 
10. Winners will be paid in Wynn Las Vegas live casino chips. 
 
11. Players will need to refer to each Event’s structure sheet for applicable details including but not limited 
to the scheduled dates of play, start times, and other relevant structure information. 
 
12. IRS Compliance requires each player provide a valid government issued ID and a social security 
number. Nonresident aliens are subject to 30% US Income Tax withholding. ITIN's are required for 
Treaty Country exemptions. Tax form W-2G will be issued to all players winning in excess of $5,000, 
net of the applicable Tournament Entry Fee. 
 
13. Wynn Las Vegas standard poker tournament rules (found at wynnpoker.com and inside the Wynn

General Terms and Conditions 
November 27 – December 21, 2026    
 
 
1. These General Poker Tournament Terms and Conditions are meant to be read and followed in conjunction 
with Wynn’s standard poker rules, and each individual Tournament event’s (may be referred to as “Event” or 
collectively as a “Tournament”) Terms and Conditions and Structure Sheet. In the event there is a conflict, 
these Terms and Conditions shall prevail. 
2. Players and guests must be at least 21 years of age. 
3. Registration for each Event will open four (4) hours prior to the scheduled start of play. Players will register 
in the Wynn Las Vegas Poker Room, located in Encore at Wynn Las Vegas. 
4. The Tournament entry fee (the “Entry Fee”) must be paid with cash or Wynn Las Vegas live casino chips; no 
other forms of payment will be accepted. 
5. All Events will use Tournament chips for play. Tournament chips have no cash value, may not be used for 
any other purpose, and must be returned to Wynn Las Vegas at the end of each Event.   
6. All Events will utilize the Big Blind Ante format unless otherwise noted on the Tournament structure sheet. In 
the event that the player in the big blind has less than the required amount to post both the big blind and the 
ante, the big blind will be posted first. The ante will then be posted with any remaining Tournament chips.  
7. A redraw for seats will occur at the conclusion of each day for all multi-flight and multi-day Events, as well as 
when each tournament reaches the final table. All Events will redraw when the Event reaches the final table.  
8. When the tournament reaches the final five (5) tables, the next table to “break” will be selected by random 
draw by the Tournament Director. This process will continue for each table thereafter until the final table 
redraw is reached.   
9. Tournament chip stacks will be put into play at the start of the event for all registered players who have been 
issued a table and seat assignment. Players registered as an “alternate” will receive a seat assignment from 
the Tournament Staff when seating becomes available.  
10. At the conclusion of the registration period, all paid entries (including alternates) who have yet to be seated 
will be assigned a seat and their Tournament chips will be put into play. 
11. A player will forfeit their option to cancel (void) their entry once their Tournament chip stack has been put 
into play and will not be entitled to a refund. 
12. Timely play is expected of all players, and stalling is not permitted. Intentional stalling in an effort to gain an 
advantage over the field is strictly prohibited and may result in a penalty, including during events that feature 
an Action Clock. The use of time extensions in unwarranted situations, specifically when players are 
approaching a pay jump, will be considered a stalling violation and may result in the forfeiture of all 
remaining time extension chips. 
13. At the sole discretion of the Tournament Director, a single hand taking considerably longer to complete than 
the rest of the field, during which time one or more players at other tables are eliminated, resulting in a pay 
jump, will result in prize money being split evenly between all players eliminated during such time. 
14. Winners will be paid in Wynn Las Vegas live casino chips. 
15. Players will need to refer to each Event’s structure sheet for applicable details including but not limited to the 
scheduled dates of play, start times, and other relevant structure information. 
16. IRS Compliance requires each player provide a valid government issued ID and a social security number. 
Nonresident aliens are subject to 30% US Income Tax withholding. ITIN's are required for Treaty Country 
exemptions. Tax form W-2G will be issued to all players winning in excess of $5,000, net of the applicable 
Tournament Entry Fee. 
17. Wynn Las Vegas standard poker rules (found inside the Wynn Poker Room) and current standard TDA rules 
(found at https://www.pokertda.com/poker-tda-rules/) apply. Where there is a conflict, these Terms will 
prevail, followed by the Wynn Las Vegas standard poker rules, the terms specific to any Event, and the TDA 
rules, in that order. 
18. Players are required to be a member of the Wynn Rewards program in order to participate in a Tournament. 
Wynn Rewards has its own terms and conditions. Please visit the Wynn Rewards desk for details. 
19. Players and guests will be required to adhere to all applicable Wynn Las Vegas policies. Wynn Resorts 
requires appropriate and respectful interactions between our guests and employees in our resorts. Wynn 
Resorts reserves the right to trespass anyone exhibiting behavior, language, or clothing, that, at our 
discretion, is inconsistent with the Wynn Resorts behavior standards. The Wynn behavior standards and 
other applicable policies can be accessed at www.wynnlasvegas.com. In the event a player or their guests 
are prevented from accessing property as a result of such policies or trespassed from property for non-
compliance with such policies, then player shall be prohibited from participating in the Event or Tournament

Players of all skill levels can join for an affordable buy-in and a shot at big prizes. Caesars Palace and its properties have some of the greatest games and best poker rooms. Every ultimate Las Vegas trip should feature unforgettable entertainment, the thrill of winning big and some good stories to take home. As luck would have it, all of these can be ticked off with one of Vegas’s oldest and greatest experiences: a poker tournament. Las Vegas is the spiritual home of poker. Playing on the Strip is a rite of passage, and nowhere is the game more refined than in a tournament. Here, it has achieved true celebrity status, with actors, sports stars, musicians and models regularly taking their seats at the felt for a share of the action. The game is so popular and glamorous, it's no surprise countless Hollywood movies have been made about it. So, when scripting your own itinerary in Las Vegas, assign some time for a poker tournament and let your main character come alive. Why is Poker So Popular in Las Vegas? Most might recognize poker in casinos as cash table games, where visitors casually dip in and out. But it is at the longer, structured poker tournaments where the real theater unfolds. Whether playing it cool with pocket rockets or pulling off an award-winning bluff, each game builds toward that unforgettable all-in moment. From beginners to aspiring World Series of Poker bracelet winners, the beauty of a poker tournament is that anyone can participate. You don’t need to be a pro or have an A-list bankroll to enter. They’re affordable to enter, easy to find and offer a fun, friendly sense of camaraderie at the card table for players of all skill levels. Choosing the Best Poker Tournament Venue in Las Vegas All poker rooms are built differently. Lighting, seating, table layouts, buy-ins and blind levels (a type of bet) are just some of the factors to look out for. Some will suit regulars, and others are more for casual players or tourists.
